 Ballon d'Or Ballon d’Or 2026: updates from 70th edition in London – live
 ⚽️ Ballon d’Or updates from 8.45pm GMT/4.45pm ET
 ⚽️ Ceremony returns to England in nod to Stanley Matthews 
 ⚽️ Women’s power rankings: will a new winner be crowned? 
 ⚽️ Send your thoughts to Daniel via email 
 LIVE  Updated  2m ago Daniel Harris Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.41 EDT First published on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.45 EDT Share Key events 2h ago Preamble 
 Favourites for the men’s award: Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé wax figures at Madame Tussauds ahead of the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London. Photograph: Ben Gregory-Ring/PA View image in fullscreen Favourites for the men’s award: Lamine Yamal, Harry Kane and Kylian Mbappé wax figures at Madame Tussauds ahead of the Ballon d'Or ceremony in London. Photograph: Ben Gregory-Ring/PA Daniel Harris Mon 26 Oct 2026 16.41 EDT First published on Mon 26 Oct 2026 14.45 EDT Share Key events 2h ago Preamble 
 1m ago 16.41 EDT “You quote Josh Goldblatt,” begins Craig Reeves. “‘How many of these candidates actually make you smile for the quality of their football and skills?’” wonders Josh Goldblatt. “‘Maybe Lamine, but the last entertainer surely was Ronaldinho, 2005 winner.’”
 “Why does it feel like these days most ‘football fans’ don’t actually like football? If you’re not entertained by Harry Kane’s quality, I’m afraid you’re watching the wrong sport. Maybe try basketball? (And I’m an Arsenal fan, so there’s no bias here!)“
 I don’t think the point is that Kane isn’t entertaining, but he’s not an entertainer, per se, but an accumulator. Similarly, post-2006-07, Cristiano Ronaldo changed from entertainer to accumulator, but he was still entertaining thereafter.
 Share 4m ago 16.38 EDT The London traffic means the ceremony has been pushed back to an 8.45pm start. Already, I’m getting strong Champions League draw vibes.
 Share 6m ago 16.36 EDT Caroline Graham Hansen also hasn’t prepared a speech, which is probably OK, brilliant though she is. I wonder, though, if we might be seeing her again next term, now Alexia has left Barca and there’s more rom for her to be the star.
 Share 9m ago 16.34 EDT I’d give him the award again just for this.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share 10m ago 16.33 EDT Lamine Yamal has arrived, and as he walks through the vestibule there’s a minor scuffle with a cameraman and security. I think we’ll need a replay there, but doubt Dazn oblige us.
 Share 12m ago 16.31 EDT “So, ‘Denis Law was a penalty-box player …’” begins Geoiff Wignall. “What? He was a No 10 who played (superbly) as a striker for the sake of the team and not so much a box to box player as byline to byline. Not many could pass the ball around Pat Jennings from 18+ yards.
 Likewise Greaves was also a 10 - and his international goals to games ratio is still better than Kane’s, without such a percentage of penalties or games against minnows. I don’t seek to disparage Kane, fine player that he is (if prone to gamesmanship), just to set the record a little straighter.”
 Denis Law a no 10? I’ve never heard such thing before. Here, in Richard Williams’ obituary, we see the words “penalty area” in both the first two paragraphs.
 Denis Law: the balletic superstar who scored with an extrovert’s flourish Read more Between 1962-63 and 68-69, he scored 29, 46, 39, 24, 25, 10 and 30 goals. That is never a no 10.
 Here’s Jonathan wilson on Greaves the no 9.
 Jimmy Greaves redefined perception of what a centre-forward should be | Jonathan Wilson Read more Share 19m ago 16.23 EDT Just realised my wife will be home in a couple of hours; yup, I’ve got to bite the bullet, sin against my soul, and put the heating back on.
 Share 22m ago 16.20 EDT What Kane said about how his teammates talk about him – what a feeling that must be. During the World Cup, it was moving to hear the England players discuss his dedication, seriousness and intensity in every single training session, and their desire to learn from him; no one has done more to maximise their talent.
 Share 26m ago 16.17 EDT Kane says he’s a bit nervous as unlike a match it’s out of his control. He’s hoping it goes his way, and has seen some friends and family. Told there’s not much more he could’ve done, he says there’s always more, and had he converted one of the Champions League and World Cup semis to silverware, he’d have taken it for sure. He backs himself as a finisher and as a creator, so with fast players around him and the way Bayern play, he’s able to drop deeper while still scoring the goals. He loves the way his teammates talk about him and hopes he wins tonight.
 View image in fullscreen Harry Kane fixes his tie. Photograph: Kin Cheung/AP Share Updated at  16.25 EDT 31m ago 16.12 EDT “I like to ask who would you pay the most to watch, rather than who is the best,” emails Fin, a bit of a follow-on from the email Josh sent regards Ronaldinho. Out of the current players my top three would be Yamal, Kvaratskhelia and Olise.”
 They are probably our foremost artists, though I also love Pedri for that. As it goes, Dembélé was once in that category, then became a more serious accumulator.
 Share 33m ago 16.10 EDT Ooooh yeah, Ousmane Dembélé takes the lead in the rig-out stakes, so cool he makes sunglasses indoors look banging. Again, photo to follow.
 Share 37m ago 16.05 EDT Harry Kane arrives, hair McDonald’s arching as it does. In an amazing turn-up for the books, his suit isn’t a slick as Mbappé’s or even close to it – photo to follow.
 View image in fullscreen Photograph: Kin Cheung/AP Share 40m ago 16.02 EDT “Joining a long line of people who say this popularity contest, leaked to you by Fabrizio, is dead to them after an injustice,” laments Jakob Mathiszig-Lee . “Nedved over Henry in 03 for me, but there’s plenty of others, Sneijder in 10 and Lewandowski in 20 and 21.”
 I agree, those Messi/Ronaldo years were suboptimal. Essentially, Nedved got it for one performance, Juve v Real Madrid in the Champions League – though I actually think Ruud van Nistelrooy would’ve won the domestic awards were the voting done later in the season.
 Share 44m ago 15.58 EDT Mbappe is in the house, looking pretty suave. Eddie Howe and Jason Tindall are surely due shortly.
 Share 46m ago 15.57 EDT “How many of these candidates actually make you smile for the quality of their football and skills?” wonders Josh Goldblatt. “Maybe Lamine, but the last entertainer surely was Ronaldinho, 2005 winner.”
 You set them up and I’ll stick them away: here’s a piece about the wonder of O Bruxo.
 Golden Goal: Ronaldinho for Barcelona v Chelsea (2005) | Daniel Harris Read more Otherwse, I think Olise is that type of player though not, of course that type of quality – perhaps yet – likewise Mbappé. I mean look at this from last week.
 Share 51m ago 15.52 EDT “Re ‘he’s the best finisher from 12-22 yards I’ve ever seen,’” begins Geoff Wignall. “I get that you’re too young to have seen Greaves, Eusebio, Best, Law or Cruyff – let alone Puskas, whom I also never saw - but are you really claiming he’s better from that range than Messi? ‘Cause he ain’t.”
 I’m too young to have seen them in the flesh, but Denis Law was a penalty-box player, likewise Greaves. Best’s goalscoring is underappreciated – from 64-65 to 71-72, he scored 14, 17, 10, 32, 22, 23, 22, 27 – but he wasn’t as deadly from the edge of the box as Kane and I don’t think Messi was either. He is as good with curlers, but not the low-backlift laces.
 Share 1h ago 15.45 EDT Luis de la Fuente tells Dazn he’d like to manage in the Premier League eventually, which is an interesting one – the job is very different to the one he’s currently killing, and building a team to play in his style would not be at all easy.
 Share 1h ago 15.43 EDT “Your rationale for Kane not winning is just weird,” reckons Emmanuel Dairo. “Lamine had perhaps the worst World Cup of a certified superstar outside maybe post-elite Ronaldo in 2022. I don’t think it’s up for debate that Kane performed better in USA than him overall. As for playing for the best team argument, so did Yamal, and I’d go as far as saying Kane being a space-vacating cenre-forward was a big part of why someone like Michael Olise blossomed. Finally, for all Mbappe’s brilliance, his efforts ultimately led to nothing for club or country, unlike Kane.”
 Olise was brilliant at Palace, which is why Bayern bought him and also brilliant for France – his performance against Senegal was better than any Kane delivered at the World Cup.
 On Lamine, I think his work in La Liga is worth more than Kane’s in the Bundesliga, and he delivered in the World Cup semi, when, I’m afraid, Kane shrunk and, on Mbappe, I can’t be differentiating Kane from him by virtue of a title won with Bayern, given they’d managed 11 in a row before he arrived and Mbappe. brilliant at the World Cup, has the explosive ability that I want in my personal concepption of what a centre-forward should be.
 Share 1h ago 15.37 EDT “The Ballon d’Or is dead to me,” writes Marek Wojenski. “In the last decade or two it’s been a public relations contest but what finally did it was the cancellation of the award in 2020.
 Lewandowski should have won it. Yes, as a Poland fan, I am bitter as we’re not likely to have another Polish candidate in my lifetime.”
 I don’t know about that – we’ve had two in mine, the other being Zibi Boniek, and three since 1974, Kazimierz Deyna the missing man.
 Share 1h ago 15.33 EDT R9, we learn, will be presenting the men’s award. He won it in 1997, when there was no doubt whatsoever as to who the best player in the world was. To this day, I’ve seen no one so shockingly brilliant, a superhuman playing an entirely different sport to the rest. Here’s a piece on what made him so special.
 Golden Goal: Ronaldo for Internazionale v Lazio (1998) | Daniel Harris Read more View image in fullscreen R9 is in the house. Photograph: Tolga Akmen/EPA Share Updated at  15.37 EDT 1h ago 15.30 EDT I’m delighted to see Barbra Banda on the shortlist. Selfishly, I’d love her to come to the WSL – I think she’d be an incredible fit. Oh, and Putellas who has joined us in the UK, is in the house; she prepared an outfit but hasn’t prepared a speech. No matter, she owns some of the most articulate feet in the world.
 Share 1h ago 15.27 EDT I can’t for the life of me get on board with the line we’re now hearing: had Argentina somehow snaffled the World Cup, the award would have to be Messi’s. He’s still got plenty, of course, but a stuffy set-piece goal, say, or a 0-0 and penalty triumph wouldn’t have somehow made him the best in the world. It’s not a lifetime achievement award.
 Share 1h ago 15.25 EDT Talking of UK winners, it’s absolutely insane to think that, in 1968, three winners – Denis Law, Bobby Charlton and George Best – played in the same Manchester United team. Now, though, despite the money in the Premier League and with the exception of Erling Haaland and Bruno Fernandes, the best attackers are found in La Liga and Ligue 1. That looks likely to change only in the next generation and only if English clubs develop their own elite talent
 View image in fullscreen George Best shows off his award in April 1968 alongside his Manchester United manager Matt Busby (second right) and teammates Bobby Charlton (centre) and Denis Law (right) who won the award in 1966 and 1964 respectively. Photograph: Mirrorpix/Alamy Share Updated at  15.35 EDT 1h ago 15.19 EDT DAZN have just interviewed Michael Owen, since the sad death of Kevin Keegan the only surviving British winner. If I’m honest, he did pretty well to get that, which isn’t to decry his efforts – in Rome and Cardiff especially – but the best player in the world? Not for me, Clive.
 View image in fullscreen 2001 Ballon d’Or winner Michael Owen and wife Louise arrive for the ceremony. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share Updated at  15.25 EDT 1h ago 15.17 EDT There appears to have been a leak: on the Ballon d’Or website, there’ve been articles lauding Kane, Mbappé and Lamine. That won’t surprise anyone, but of course the order is what really matters.
 Share 1h ago 15.16 EDT “Team PSG, Manager Luis Enrique, Ballon D’Or Harry Kane,” reckons Krishnamoorthy V. “Have Real Madrid decided to be present this year?”
 Isn’t is sweet of them?
 Share 1h ago 15.14 EDT Lamine will, we have to assume, win the young player away for the third time on the spin. I think we can confidently say he was the best 16-year-old we’ve ever seen though, once he turned 17, Pelé had him beat.
 Share 2h ago 15.12 EDT Why, then, am I not going for Kane, seeing as you don’t ask. It’s a strange one given he’s the best finisher from 12-22 yards I’ve ever seen, and has reinvented his position, a prolific goalscorer but also a playmaker. However throughout his career, he’s not quite done it in the biggest games, and I just can’t anoint him the planet’s best for this season when he couldn’t get it done in the closing stages of either World Cup or Champions League – again. Killing the Bundesliga in by far its best team, even without him, and a brace against DR Congo, just isn’t enough, and ultimately, that’s why I’m going for Lamine – though, if you asked me who I think the best player in the world is, I’d probably say Mbappé, just.
 Share 2h ago 15.08 EDT So who should win? In the women’s competition, I’m going for the wondrous Alexia Putellas; I’m not sure many will argue to the contrary.
 The men’s competition is a harder choice. I can’t decide between Kylian Mbappé and Lamine Yamal, but I’m going for Lamine because he inspired Barcelona to the title and was easily the better of the two in the World Cup semi; in third, I’d go for Michael Olise, but I’m sure Harry Kane will be on the podium.
 Share 2h ago 15.04 EDT Should anyone fancy learning even more about Sir Stan, here’s a piece about him and the nature of heroism .
 Share 2h ago 15.03 EDT So who’s going to win? Well, first things first: the ceremony is being held in London to honour Stanley Matthews, who won the debut award 70 years ago.
 Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews Read more View image in fullscreen The family of Sir Stanley Matthews, including son Stanley Matthews Jr (second left), daughter Jean Matthews (third left) and granddaughters Mandy Bray (third right) and Samantha Davis (second right) pictured on the red carpet ahead of the ceremony. Photograph: Adam Davy/PA Share Updated at  15.10 EDT 2h ago 14.45 EDT Preamble
 One of the things we love about football is that, in a fickle world of questions, it offers us definitive answers. The best team in the league is the team which wins the league; in order to be certain who deserves to win a match, we’ve devised a handy metric to tell us, known as the score; and should we ever be unsure as to what silly haircut we should have next, what histrionic we should practise, or how best to flout authority, the beautiful game will surely supply us with an answer.
 The Ballon d’Or, though, is a different state of affairs. Though the game offers us no parameters for judgment, it being a team sport, often it’s obvious which players have been the world’s best over a season. On other occasions, though, it’s a matter of criteria and opinion, which is where we find ourselves this evening.
 But this term, we’ve no outstanding candidate on either men’s or women’s side, which allows us to enjoy plenty of conjecture and opinion, deconstructing this wonderful thing of ours to examine its constituent parts. Are we honouring the best or the most effective? Should we be looking for reliability or inspiration, impact or output, consistent excellence or big-game decisiveness? The next few hours will tell us what one journalist from each of the top 100 countries in the Fifa rankings think but, something else we love about football is that whenever decision is made and whatever it is, there’ll always be people desperate to tell those responsible why they’re wrong. Let’s do it!
 Showtime: 7pm GMT
